description: Traceability matrix of section 13.5: fixtures to contracts to tests to milestones. Two checks in InterCat.Architecture.Tests keep it honest.

fixtures.title: Seeded two-process TCP loopback exchange
fixtures.scenario: Section 13.1 scenario 1: TCP IPv4 loopback, several connections, several messages per connection.

truth.independence: Both processes write their own log from ordinary socket calls; neither reads InterCat state.

expected.note: The expected query bundle and its canonical hash are defined by IC-018. This milestone records measured counters and the inputs they came from.

environment.result: All six section 14.2 criteria met at 100%: 48 of 48 truth operations observed, bound to a flow instance and byte-measured, 0 false peer attributions of 4, 2 of 2 connections discovered and 4 of 4 memberships resolved. Truth and observed transport both 28,527 B sent. Tier TrafficVisualization, promoted once ADR-007 put this build in the section 1.3 matrix; the counters are unchanged from the first measured run.

fixtures.title: Local RPC calls to the Windows service control manager
fixtures.scenario: Section 13.1 scenario 5: local RPC with a known client, a Windows service host as the server, and the fixture run twice inside one capture.

truth.independence: The client logs every call it issues through the documented service API; it never reads InterCat state. The server is a Windows service host, which the scenario file states explicitly.

expected.note: 8 of 8 calls observed and bound to the expected interface with their completions paired, no byte domain on any descriptor, and no client-to-server peer paired. Tier ExperimentalEvidence; scope recorded in ADR-004.

environment.result: 8 of 8 truth calls observed, bound to the expected interface and completion-paired, reproduced across two runs in one capture. Tier ExperimentalEvidence on a supported build: the gaps are the source’s, not the build’s - no byte domain on any descriptor and no interface lifetime (ADR-004).

fixtures.title: Process, resource and clock identity collisions
fixtures.scenario: Section 7.2 and 8.1: PID and resource-key reuse, a late record carrying the earlier start key, an equal key on another host, and a fixed QPC conversion.

truth.independence: The input contains only fixed source identities, lifetimes and native clock values; it does not depend on InterCat output.

expected.note: Expected relationships are deliberately semantic: distinct, first epoch, or unresolved. They do not bless a platform-specific object address or wall-clock guess.

environment.result: The pure domain fixture passes without Windows, ETW or UI dependencies.

fixtures.title: Callback envelope admission, extended data and clock replay probe
fixtures.scenario: Sections 18.1–18.2: known metadata, an unknown schema with opaque bytes, known content under a metadata-only policy, header-only evidence, allowlisted and denied extended items, a real EVENT_RECORD extended-data array read in bounded copies, and the capture source clock persisted with the file. The IC-009 harness then drives a declared load series through both evidence variants, so the bounded queue reaches its limit and the writer becomes the pacing stage.

truth.independence: The corpus declares original bytes and policy inputs before admission; expected dispositions are stored separately.

expected.note: All four headers remain attributable. Only approved metadata survives; unknown and content bodies and a denied extended item have explicit omission outcomes; an over-long extended item keeps its original length; and the persisted source clock replays byte-for-byte.

environment.result: Two five-level elevated series on a supported build. The call-stack series reports decisionReady: true with no blockers: identical ordered replay at every level, 74,682 of 74,682 extended items copied, persisted and replayed, the queue bound reached with 71,107 counted drops and zero loss, and the writer pacing at 104% of an acquisition window. ADR-008 is accepted on this evidence.

The version-0 probe round-trips admitted identity, extended items and the source clock descriptor, excludes unapproved bodies and denied extended types, and rejects checksum corruption. The extended-data walker is asserted against a synthetic EVENT_RECORD, not against a live capture. It is not journal-v1 or an ETL comparison. The load series, its saturation classifier and the storage probe arithmetic are asserted portably; the elevated runs they describe are recorded under bench/results/.

provenance.contents: Synthetic headers, schemas, content markers, extended items, a synthetic EVENT_RECORD layout and expected policy dispositions.
